To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have cloned, sequenced, and characterized the mouse Copb cDNA, and mapped the mouse Copb locus to mouse Chr 8.

the mouse Copb cDNA was determined by overlapping EST contigs and EST walking, and the gene was mapped to chromosome 7 at a distance of 53. 3 centimorgan (cM) from the centromere by using the mouse radiation hybrid panel.
the mouse Copb cDNA was determined by EST walking and the Copb gene was located at mouse Chr 7 by RH mapping, and the Copb cDNA and gene are highly conserved in rat and human.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new mouse model for the study of the COPI-coated transport vesicles.
the identification of the ru2 candidate gene,
the cloning and characterization of the mouse beta-COP gene, which may be a useful tool to investigate the function of COPI-coated transport vesicles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Copb gene does not encode the mouse ru2 gene.
the ru2 gene does not encode the beta subunit (Copb) of the COPI coat protein complex.
the Copb gene is not the ru2 gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the Copb gene and mapped the mouse gene to a position of 7B2.5-7B3.1.
the Copb gene is an essential gene in mouse, and it is not the candidate gene of ru2.
Copb is a candidate gene for ru1, a mouse model of Hermansky-Puddlak syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mouse beta-COP gene is a useful model to understand the function of human beta-COP in the COPI complex.
the Copb gene is a useful tool in studying the function of COPI-coated transport vesicles.
Copb is a highly conserved gene in mouse and other mammalian species, which is likely to be a candidate gene for other mouse mutants with coatamer-related defects.
